answer: On the toy one-way network the drive time from A to C is 2.0 minutes (A-B 1 + B-C 1, via the one-way street). From C to A it is 5.0 minutes. The one-way B-C street cannot be driven C to B, so the route takes the 5-minute A-C detour (2.5 + 2.5). That is the asymmetry expected for a one-way edge, and both values match the known answer. I built the toy network with the same pro/network.py build_network code that builds the NYC network, using a Minutes cost with negative values meaning no travel, and solved with an Origin-Destination cost matrix. I did not rebuild the NYC network. I confirmed the cached C:\proveit_work\fire_ems.gdb network exists (112,711 drivable segments, Length and Minutes costs).
traps_or_caveats: The toy check validates one-way handling only; it is a unit test, not NYC drive times.
One-way is encoded as a negative FT_Min/TF_Min cost, so the field direction must match the digitized direction of each line.
The NYC network was reused from cache (fire_ems.gdb), not rebuilt; I only checked that it exists and has Length and Minutes costs.
NYC costs assume posted speed (default speeds where missing), with no traffic or siren speed-up, so they are not real-world drive times.
The stock pro/check_network.py writes outputs/check_network.json, outside my folder, so I wrote my own script with the same logic and a T01_toy.gdb scratch gdb.
The OD matrix also returns A->A and C->C at 0.0, which are trivial.
